  "single_defensible_answer": true,
  "source_support": true,
  "numeric_solution": false,
  "boundary_cases": true,
  "passage_integrity": true,
  "passage_answerability": true,
  "meaningfully_distinct": true,
  "evidence_ids": ["E1.1", "E2.1", "E3.1"],
  "reasons": [
    "Under a fixed exchange rate system, an official government action that raises the exchange rate (making foreign currency costlier and domestic currency cheaper) is defined by NCERT as devaluation.",
    "Revaluation refers to an official decrease in the exchange rate making domestic currency costlier, while appreciation and floating exchange rates pertain to market-determined regimes."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Balance of Payments",
  "syllabus_topic": "Foreign exchange rate - fixed and flexible exchange rates",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "The regime is a fixed exchange rate system where government sets or revises the official rate.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "The exchange rate is defined as the price of foreign currency in units of domestic currency (Rs per dollar increases from 75 to 80).",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "NCERT Macroeconomics defines an official increase in the fixed exchange rate as devaluation.",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": ["E3.1"]
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "The government deliberately decreased the exchange rate to make domestic currency costlier in a fixed exchange rate system.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "The currency's value changed due to market forces in a flexible exchange rate regime.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "The government abandoned the fixed peg and allowed market supply and demand to freely set the exchange rate.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly tests foreign exchange rate terminology (fixed exchange rates and devaluation) from Unit V Open Economy Macroeconomics."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard single-response four-option MCQ format identical to CUET UG economics questions."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Direct conceptual recall and comprehension from NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics chapter 6."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Distractors target common student confusions between devaluation, revaluation, and appreciation."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 1,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "recall",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": []
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Revaluation of the rupee",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E3.1",
      "premise_quote": "On the other hand, a Revaluation is said to occur, when the Government decreases the exchange rate (thereby, making domestic currency costlier) in a fixed exchange rate system.",
      "reason": "Revaluation requires the government to decrease the exchange rate, whereas here the rate increased from 75 to 80."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E3.1",
      "premise_quote": "In a fixed exchange rate system, when some government action increases the exchange rate (thereby, making domestic currency cheaper) is called Devaluation.",
      "reason": "The government action increased the exchange rate from Rs 75 to Rs 80 per dollar, which is devaluation."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Appreciation of the rupee",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E2.1",
      "premise_quote": "Similarly, in a flexible exchange rate regime, when the price of domestic currency (rupees) in terms of foreign currency (dollars) increases, it is called Appreciation of the domestic currency (rupees) in terms of foreign currency (dollars).",
      "reason": "Appreciation occurs in a flexible exchange rate regime and refers to domestic currency gaining value."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Floating of the exchange rate",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "This exchange rate is determined by the market forces of demand and supply. It is also known as Floating Exchange Rate .",
      "reason": "Floating exchange rates are determined by market forces rather than fixed peg adjustments by the government."
    }
  ]
}
